VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Meta.Description: Single source of truth for every material property used by the 2D preview fills and the 3D PBR renderer. Nothing here is duplicated in Na__Env3d__Config.json or VghLantern__AppConfig__Main__.json.
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Meta.MigrationNote: Finish palette migrated out of VghLantern__AppConfig__Main__.json and the role colours out of Na__Env3d__Config.json VghLantern__Env3d__Config__Materials. AppCore__ConfigLoader derives the legacy FinishOptions section from the Finishes array below, so existing option-list consumers read this file without knowing it moved.
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Meta.PaletteNote: THREE selectable palettes, one per element that is actually specified separately. Finishes is the frame. CapFinishes is the glaze bar cap, outside the roof. JoineryFinishes is the glaze bar trim, inside the room. They are separate arrays rather than one list with tags because a cap is never offered an interior eggshell and the trim is never offered a powder coat, and a single list would have to be filtered at every call site to say so.
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Meta.RenderModelNote: Metalness / Roughness workflow. ClearCoat above zero promotes the material to a THREE.MeshPhysicalMaterial, which is what gives powder coat its thin lacquer sheen over a matt pigment layer, and at a much lower value the soft broad sheen of an eggshell joinery paint.

VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Finish.Name: Anthracite Grey
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Finish.HexColorNote: The true RAL 7016 swatch. This is the value the 2D preview fill and the specification schedule use, so it must stay accurate to the paint reference and must not be lightened to flatter the 3D view.
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Finish.RenderAlbedoHexNote: OPTIONAL 3D-only override. A swatch photograph is a dark paint chip measured under studio light; a renderer instead wants diffuse albedo, and for a dark powder coat that sits lighter than the chip because the real surface scatters light off its micro-texture in a way a single flat colour cannot. Without this the frame renders closer to black than a real RAL 7016 lantern ever looks. Raise toward #545B61 to lift the frame further, or delete the key to render the raw swatch.
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Finish.Description: Vale's standard contemporary finish. Satin polyester powder coat over marine grade aluminium, colour matched to RAL 7016.

VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Finish.Name: White Painted
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Finish.RalReference: Off white - nearest RAL 9010 Pure White
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Finish.Description: A timeless warm off white rather than a stark brilliant white - it sits with painted joinery and stonework instead of fighting them. Satin polyester powder coat over marine grade aluminium.

VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Finish.Name: Lead
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Finish.Description: Natural metal rather than a coating, so it carries real metalness and a duller broken reflection. The tone is weathered lead, not bright cast lead.

VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Finish.FallbackNote: Used only when a lantern stores a finish name that is no longer in the palette above. A neutral coated aluminium tone, deliberately not matching any real product.

VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config.VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__CapFin: The glaze bar cap is the decorative capping seen from OUTSIDE the roof, and it is specified on its own rather than following the frame. The frame is painted joinery and the outside of the roof carries lead flashing, so the frame colour has no bearing on what the cap is finished in. Powder Coated Aluminium is the standard and is what a cap is supplied in unless a job says otherwise.

VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__CapFin.Name: Powder Coated Aluminium
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__CapFin.RenderAlbedoHexNote: 3D-only lift, for the reason given on the frame finish of the same coating: a dark paint chip measured under studio light is not diffuse albedo, and rendering the raw swatch puts the cap closer to black than a real one ever looks.
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__CapFin.FlatShadingNote: Matches the core and the trim, so the three parts of one bar shade alike.
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__CapFin.Description: The standard Vale cap. Satin polyester powder coat over the extruded aluminium capping.

VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__CapFin.Name: White
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__CapFin.RalReference: Off white - nearest RAL 9010 Pure White
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__CapFin.Description: A warm off white rather than a stark brilliant white, so the roof lines read soft against sky.

VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__CapFin.Name: Lead
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__CapFin.Description: Natural metal rather than a coating, so it carries real metalness and a duller broken reflection. Sits with the lead flashing that dresses the outside of the roof.

VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config.VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner: The glaze bar trim is INTERNAL joinery - it is the moulding seen from inside the room, and it is either left as natural timber or painted. Every paint below is an EGGSHELL, which is the sheen interior joinery is specified in: it holds a soft broad highlight and nothing more. Nothing here should ever be given a gloss response. ClearCoat is deliberately near zero with a high ClearCoatRoughness, which is what a low sheen paint film actually does to light; raising ClearCoat toward 0.3 or dropping Roughness below 0.4 would turn these into the gloss paint this note exists to prevent.

VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Name: Natural Douglas Fir
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.UsesMaterialNote: Resolves to the Timber role material below rather than restating it, so bare douglas fir is described in exactly one place.
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Description: The trim left bare: clear finished softwood, no pigment.

VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Name: Neutral White
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.PaintReference: Neutral white - nearest RAL 9010 Pure White
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.HexColorNote: A soft neutral white with a trace of warmth. Deliberately not a brilliant white, which reads blue under rooflight and fights painted walls.
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Substrate: Eggshell joinery paint on douglas fir
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.EnvMapIntensityNote: Low, matching the natural timber it replaces. The trim faces into the room and away from the sky the environment map is built from, so a strong reflection would read as wet paint.
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Description: House neutral white. The safe choice where the joinery is meant to disappear.

VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Name: Farrow and Ball French Gray
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.HexColorNote: A grey with a green cast rather than a blue one, which is what stops it going cold against timber and stone.
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Substrate: Eggshell joinery paint on douglas fir
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Description: The house default, and the most forgiving of the four. Reads as a warm putty in low light and as a soft green-grey in full sun, so it sits with almost any room below it.

VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Name: Farrow and Ball Card Room Green
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.PaintReference: Farrow & Ball No.79 Card Room Green
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.HexColorNote: A dark sage carrying a good deal of grey. Strong enough to frame the glass without going black in the corners of the room.
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Substrate: Eggshell joinery paint on douglas fir
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Description: The traditional garden room green. Sits with planting seen through the glass rather than against it.

VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Name: Farrow and Ball Pigeon
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.HexColorNote: A mid blue-green grey. The lightest of the coloured four, so it keeps a divided roof from reading heavy.
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Substrate: Eggshell joinery paint on douglas fir
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Description: Quiet and slightly cool. Works where the room below already has a strong wall colour.

VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Name: Farrow and Ball Railings
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.HexColorNote: Near black with a blue cast, never a true black. This is the swatch value and is what a schedule quotes.
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.RenderAlbedoHexNote: 3D-only lift, same reasoning as the dark powder coat: rendering the raw chip puts the trim closer to black than a painted moulding looks in a real room.
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Substrate: Eggshell joinery paint on douglas fir
VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Joiner.Description: The contemporary choice. Draws the bar set as a graphic grid against the sky.

Glazing.Description: Clear double glazed unit. Ported from ValeVision3D MaxEngine, which resolves MAT101__Glass__ClearDefault out of the shared Na__Common__DataLib__CoreSuEntityStandards materials index and then applies its glass environment overrides on top. The values below are that same recipe, so a lantern and a ValeVision scene render glass identically.
Glazing.HexColorNote: rgb(230, 240, 255) - the DataLib base, near white with the faintest blue cast. This is NOT what you see on screen; it is the tint the reflection is filtered through after BrightnessMultiplier below has taken it almost to black.
Glazing.BrightnessMultiplierNote: THE KEY VALUE, and the one that looks like a mistake. 1/4096. The base colour is multiplied down to effectively black so the diffuse term contributes nothing and EVERY visible thing about the glass comes from the environment reflection instead. Glass painted as a flat translucent blue reads as tinted acrylic no matter what the opacity is; glass that is black plus a reflection reads as glass. Raise toward 0.01 only if you want a deliberately tinted unit.
Glazing.OpacityNote: Opacity multiplies the whole shaded result, reflection included, so on a near-black base it behaves as a reflection strength dial as much as a transparency one. 0.2 is the DataLib default and reads faint on a lantern seen against bright sky; 0.3 gives the pane more presence without closing the view through it.
Glazing.RoughnessNote: Sharper than the DataLib default of 0.05. A crisp reflection is what sells a flat pane; blur it and the glass turns milky.
Glazing.MetalnessNote: Glass is a dielectric. The reflection arrives through the standard 4 percent Fresnel term, which is what gives the pane its grazing-angle brightening - raising metalness would make it read as a mirror rather than a window.
Glazing.EnvMapIntensityNote: Effective reflection strength of the glass. Glass inherits scene.environment like everything else - it has to, because the material is shared across surfaces that each have their own context-specific radiance map - so this value is divided by the scene Environment Intensity when applied. That keeps this number meaning what it says and leaves the frame dial free to move without dragging the glass with it.
Glazing.DepthWriteNote: Off, so panes do not z-fight each other in a scene with no order independent transparency.

BuildersUpstand.Note: The builders kerb is a GRP covered upstand, so it takes the GRP material below rather than carrying a colour of its own. Point this at another role key to change what the kerb is finished in.

Grp.Description: Glass reinforced plastic. The material of the builders kerb and any flat roof area abutting the lantern. Laid wet over ply and rolled out by hand, so it is never optically flat - the surface carries a fine granular texture from the chopped strand mat under the topcoat, plus a soft undulation from the roller.
Grp.HexColorNote: Standard light grey GRP roofing topcoat, very slightly warm so it sits against the powder coated frame rather than competing with it.
Grp.RoughnessNote: A resin topcoat is satin, not matt: it holds a broad soft highlight rather than a sharp one.
Grp.EnvMapIntensityNote: Held below the frame's so the kerb sits back visually and the eye goes to the lantern above it.
Grp.BumpScaleNote: Bump height in world units, so this is metres: 0.0022 is roughly two millimetres of apparent relief. Enough to break the highlight up and kill the plastic CAD look; raise toward 0.004 for a coarser hand laid finish, drop to 0.001 for a sprayed one.
Grp.BumpRepeatNote: Tiles per world unit. ExtrudeGeometry gives this mesh UVs in metres, so 26 puts one noise tile in roughly every 38 mm and the grain reads at true scale regardless of how large the lantern is.
Grp.NoiseOctavesNote: Four doublings gives both the broad roller undulation and the fine mat speckle in one map.
Grp.NoisePersistenceNote: Amplitude falloff per octave. Higher keeps more fine detail and reads grittier; lower reads smoother and more sprayed.
Grp.NoiseSeedNote: Any integer. Fixed rather than random so the same grain appears on every reload and in every exported snapshot - two screenshots of one lantern must not differ.

MillAluminium.Description: Bare mill finish aluminium. The concealed glaze bar core extrusion, which is never coated because it is never seen once the cap and trim are on. In the structural view it is the ONLY thing on screen, so it has to read unmistakably as bare metal rather than as another grey.
MillAluminium.HexColorNote: Bright and slightly cool. On a metal this is a REFLECTANCE tint, not a paint colour - at metalness 1 the diffuse term vanishes and this value tints the reflection instead, so it has to sit far brighter than the equivalent painted grey or the metal renders near black.
MillAluminium.RoughnessNote: The base value the grain map modulates around. Raised from 0.30, which returned the environment map so sharply that a bar picked up whole recognisable patches of sky and ground and read as chrome rather than as aluminium. Mill stock is satin: the surroundings should be present in it but never legible.
MillAluminium.MetalnessNote: Just off a full conductor. A real extrusion carries a thin oxide film within minutes of leaving the die, and that small diffuse floor is what stops the metal collapsing toward black wherever the environment happens to be dark. Do not drop this far - below about 0.8 the diffuse term takes over and the metal turns to grey plastic.
MillAluminium.EnvMapIntensityNote: Brought down from 1.6. Bare metal does return its surroundings where a powder coat scatters them, but at 1.6 with a sharp roughness the reflection was brighter than the lit surfaces around it, which is the specific thing that reads as fake. The metal is now separated from the coated frame by the SHAPE of its highlight rather than by sheer intensity.
MillAluminium.FlatShadingNote: The section is a faceted extrusion and is meant to read as one. Flat shading keeps every arris crisp without splitting a single vertex, which is what lets the solid stay welded and manifold for the boolean pass.
MillAluminium.GrainNote: Die lines down the length of the extrusion, applied as a roughness map. This is the anisotropy: the lines vary across the bar and hold steady along it, so the highlight stretches lengthways exactly as it does on real drawn stock. Standard PBR has no true anisotropy term, and a directional roughness map is how the effect is reached without one.
MillAluminium.GrainLineDensityNote: Independent lines across one texture tile. With the repeat below this lands roughly one line every 0.15 mm, which is the right order for a die-drawn surface.
MillAluminium.GrainWanderNote: How much a line fades and strengthens over its run. Zero reads as machined rather than drawn.
MillAluminium.GrainRepeatUNote: Tiles across the section perimeter. The mesh carries UVs in world units, so this is tiles per world unit measured round the section.
MillAluminium.GrainRepeatVNote: Tiles along the bar. Held at 1: the grain is meant to run unbroken down the length, and repeating it there would print visible bands across the bar.
MillAluminium.GrainRoughnessNote: The grain map is remapped into this band by roughness x map. The spread is what produces the stretched lengthways highlight; too narrow and the metal goes flat, too wide and it reads as dirty. Moved up with the base roughness so the band still straddles it - the shape of the highlight is preserved, only its sharpness came down.
MillAluminium.GrainBumpScaleNote: A whisper of physical relief in world units, so this is metres. Die lines are microns deep in reality - this is here to catch a grazing highlight, not to be seen as texture.

Timber.Description: Douglas fir, unpainted. The glaze bar trim as supplied, seen from inside the room.
Timber.ReachedByNote: Nothing asks for this role by name. The JoineryFinishes palette entry 'Natural Douglas Fir' declares UsesMaterial: 'Timber' and is resolved to this block, so bare fir is described here once and chosen up there alongside the paints that replace it.
Timber.HexColorNote: Warm mid tan. Douglas fir runs pinker and more golden than oak, and this sits at the finished rather than the freshly machined end of its range.
Timber.RoughnessNote: A factory finished softwood moulding holds a soft sheen. Well short of a lacquered surface, well short of bare timber.
Timber.EnvMapIntensityNote: Low. The trim faces into the room, away from the sky the environment map is built from, so a strong reflection would read as wet.
Timber.FlatShadingNote: Matches the core and cap so the three parts of one bar shade alike.

SkeletonLine.Note: Line mode member colour. A line material carries no PBR response.

Component.Note: Library components - finials, bases, cresting, vents - are supplied in the same powder coated finish as the frame, so their material is resolved from the lantern's chosen finish rather than carrying its own colour.

VghLantern__PbrMaterials__Config__Previe.Note: The 2D elevation fills tint from the same HexColor the 3D material uses, so the drawing and the model can never disagree about what colour a lantern is.
